messages.content: Rewrite plain English in the manner of Hegel's writing, as his nineteenth-century English translators render it. Keep the content exactly: every claim, example and step, in the same order, and add nothing.

Rewrite in Hegel's manner:

The hawker's papers lie in the dust, their headlines a chaos of trains and thefts that do not touch the bone-deep hunger of my own particular existence. I have six rupees, a sum so trivial it is almost an insult to the concept of currency, yet it is the entirety of my power over the material world. To read is to suspend the demand of the stomach; I must extract the universal from these particular cries before the sun climbs higher and the need for sustenance becomes a tyranny I cannot philosophize away.
